newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice prices steady to firmer; focus on flood.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice prices steady to firmer; focus on flood.

text.p: Thai rice prices were steady to slightly firmer this week as the market watched closely for flood damage on rice crops, trade sources said on Thursday.
The industry was divided over the extent of damage with some expressing concerns but others expecting no sharp drop in output despite rising waters.
"Flood is better than drought. Rice paddy in lowlands is definitely affected by floods, but at the same time the output in highlands is likely to rise," one trader said.

"The rice output is likely to drop, but not sharply. I hope the floods will not put further pressure on rice prices. They are already a bit too expensive," said another. The thin market was pressured by news of the floods, trade sources said.
Thai benchmark 100 percent grade B rice was quoted around US$330-340 per tonne FOB Bangkok, compared with $320-340 per tonne last week.
According to the Interior Ministry's figure, 556,919 hectares (1.4 million acres) of farmland was damaged by floods, 397,859 (990,000 acres) of which were rice fields.
Exporters bought to cover immediate needs as only several ships were at Bangkok port loading rice to be shipped to China, Syria, Africa and Hong Kong. -- Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
